info.title: Raffa API
info.description:
Contract for the Raffa backend API (backend/src/Raffa.Api), consumed by the web (this file) and mobile (ADR-013) TypeScript clients per ADR-012's "single OpenAPI document -> one generated TypeScript client, no hand-written divergent DTOs" rule (see reports/architecture/draft/client-architect/api-consumption.md #1).

Provenance / interim status (task E01/F07/US01/T02): the API host does not yet self-publish this document -- no Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi / Swashbuckle / NSwag is wired into backend/src/Raffa.Api/Program.cs as of this task, and adding that is outside this task's file scope (the web client only; this task's frontmatter is target_repo: raffa-web). Until a backend task adds self-published OpenAPI generation, this file is hand-authored to describe exactly the routes Program.cs actually implements today, cross-checked against backend/tests/Raffa.Api.Tests. It is the single file `npm run generate:api` (web/scripts/generate-api-client.mjs) reads to produce web/src/api/generated/schema.ts, and must grow endpoint-by-endpoint as backend/src/Raffa.Api/Program.cs grows -- then be replaced outright once the API self-publishes its own document.

URL versioning (OQ-client-007 in reports/open-questions.md, still `open` at council-close: "OpenAPI codegen tool and URL versioning scheme ... owned by software-architect") is deliberately NOT applied to the paths below: Program.cs maps bare `/health`, not `/v1/health`, and a client generated against a path the API does not actually serve would 404 in every real environment. `info.version` above tracks this document's own revision; add a URL path prefix here only once software-architect fixes one and Program.cs actually serves it under that prefix.

Codegen tool choice (also part of OQ-client-007, resolved here for this task rather than left blocking it, per reports/open-questions.md's "add an entry, state the assumption, build against it"): third-party OpenAPI-to-TypeScript generators evaluated at authoring time (openapi-typescript@7.13.0, which peer-depends on `typescript@^5.x`) hard-conflict with this repo's already-committed `typescript@^7.0.2` (web/package.json, task E01/F07/US01/T01) under npm's default strict peer resolution. Rather than force an incorrect peer resolution (`--legacy-peer-deps`/`--force`) or downgrade a previous task's already-committed TypeScript version, this contract is compiled by a small first-party generator (web/scripts/generate-api-client.mjs, zero new dependencies) that reads this JSON file and emits the `paths`/`operations` TypeScript types the same way the mainstream tools shape them. Swap in a third-party tool once one publishes TypeScript-7-compatible peer ranges; the generated *output shape* (`paths`/`operations`) is deliberately kept compatible with that ecosystem convention so the swap is mechanical.

Task E06/F01/US01/T01 (typescript-client-regen) added the four operations below beyond `/health`: `POST /api/workspaces` (create), `POST /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/invites` (invite), `POST /api/documents` (upload), `GET /api/documents/{id}` (read back) -- exactly epic-06-web-foundation's own R0 scope ("the sign-in -> workspace picker flow ... and the R0 surfaces (members & roles, document upload, document-status read-back)"). backend/src/Raffa.Api/Program.cs now also maps many more routes added by backend epics E02-E05 (GET /api/contracts, GET/PATCH /api/contracts/{id}, GET /api/contracts/{id}/corrections, GET /api/renewals and /api/renewals/{contractId}/priority, POST /api/renewals/{id}/action, GET/PATCH /api/savings and GET /api/savings/kpis, POST /api/chat/query, POST /api/quotes and GET /api/quotes/{id}/assessment, POST /api/negotiations/outcomes) that this task deliberately did NOT add here: epic-06-web-foundation's own "Out of scope" list names exactly that set ("portfolio, Contract 360, review, Ask, renewals, savings, quote check -- later web epics"), and feature-01-typescript-client-regen's own "Council decisions carried into this story" calls this a "Repeating chore" -- whichever web epic first builds a screen against one of those endpoints should extend this file next, the same way this task extended the `/health`-only version task E01/F07/US01/T02 left behind. Nullable fields (e.g. a freshly-uploaded or not-yet-classified document's `contractId`) use OpenAPI 3.1's `type: [X, "null"]` union instead of a bolted-on `nullable: true` flag; web/scripts/generate-api-client.mjs gained one small, additive case for it (a `type` array renders as the equivalent TypeScript union, plus a case for `object`/`properties` -- every new response below is a flat, single-level object) -- see that script's own comments on the change.

Task E07/F03/US01/T01 (field-review-correction, ADR-020 screen 6) added `PATCH /api/contracts/{id}` (`correctContract`) and `GET /api/contracts/{id}/corrections` (`getCorrectionHistory`) -- the third web epic to extend this document (task E07/F01/US01/T01 was the first, task E07/F02/US01/T01 the second; see this paragraph's own 'repeating chore' provenance note above). Both operations were already implemented by backend task E02/F05/US01/T01/T02 (us-01-correction-history) and already named in this document's own provenance paragraph's backend-routes list ('GET/PATCH /api/contracts/{id}, GET /api/contracts/{id}/corrections') as not yet documented here -- this task closes that gap, it does not add new backend behaviour. Both response/request bodies use the same plain-object/array shapes generate-api-client.mjs already supports; no generator change was needed.

Task E08/F01/US01/T01 (renewal-pipeline, ADR-020 screen 8) added `POST /api/renewals/{id}/action` (`postRenewalAction`) -- the fourth web epic to extend this document (task E07/F01/US01/T01 was the first, E07/F02/US01/T01 the second, E07/F03/US01/T01 the third; see this paragraph's own 'repeating chore' provenance note above). This operation was already named in this document's own provenance paragraph's backend-routes list ('POST /api/renewals/{id}/action') as not yet documented here -- this task closes that gap, it does not add new backend behaviour. Already implemented by backend task E03/F03/US01/T02 (renewal-action). The 200 response's `status` field is a real, closed three-value enum (NotStarted/InProgress/Completed, RenewalActionStatus.ToString()) so it is declared with `enum` the same way GET /api/renewals's own `status` field already is -- generate-api-client.mjs renders it as a TypeScript string-literal union with no generator change needed. The request body (owner/status/action, all free-form strings on the wire) is hand-written in src/api/client.ts, like every other write operation's request type in this document -- the generator does not parse `requestBody` at all (see this file's own 'Codegen tool choice' paragraph above).

Task E08/F03/US01/T01 (quote-check-ui, ADR-018 route /quotes/:id, ADR-020 screen 10) adds the four operations this document's own provenance paragraph above named as deliberately deferred: `POST /api/quotes` (uploadQuote), `GET /api/quotes/{id}/assessment` (getQuoteAssessment), `POST /api/quotes/{id}/assessment/recalculate` (recalculateQuoteAssessment), and `POST /api/negotiations/outcomes` (captureNegotiationOutcome) -- the fourth and, for this document, last web epic to extend this file (task E07/F01/US01/T01 was the first, E07/F02/US01/T01 the second, E07/F03/US01/T01 the third; see this paragraph's own 'repeating chore' provenance note above). All four operations were already implemented by backend epic E05 (Raffa.Quotes module, wired into Program.cs via AddQuotesModule/MapQuotesEndpoints/MapNegotiationsEndpoints) before this task started; this task only documents and wraps them, it does not add new backend behaviour. `position` (Raffa.Quotes.Domain.MarketPosition) is deliberately typed as a bare nullable string, not a nullable enum -- the same generate-api-client.mjs#renderSchemaType 'enum drops the null union member' limitation getPortfolio's own `risk` field and Contract 360's `header.risk`/`clauses[].riskLevel` already worked around; web/src/api/client.ts names the real 3-value set as its own hand-written `QuoteMarketPosition` alias plus an `isQuoteMarketPosition` guard, the same pattern `PortfolioRiskSeverity`/`isPortfolioRiskSeverity` already establish. `GET /api/quotes/{id}/assessment` and `POST /api/quotes/{id}/assessment/recalculate` share an identical per-line assessment shape, duplicated rather than `$ref`'d (the generator has no `$ref`/`oneOf` support -- see its own header comment). Two operations' 404s carry a real string body (`Results.NotFound(result.Error)`, not the bare empty-body `Results.NotFound()` every earlier 404 in this document uses) -- documented with `content` accordingly, and web/src/api/client.ts reads that body instead of fabricating a generic not-found message, unlike its own earlier 404 handlers. `Raffa.Quotes.Application.Strategy.NegotiationStrategyService` (negotiation-lever recommendations + evidence, task E05/F03/US01/T01) has no HTTP endpoint anywhere in `Program.cs` -- a genuine, pre-existing backend gap this task's `raffa-web` file scope cannot close; `POST /api/negotiations/outcomes`'s own description above names it, and web/src/routes/quotes/ renders an honest gap notice in its place rather than inventing lever evidence to match the cited prototype's own fixture data.

Task E08/F02/US01/T01 (savings-home, ADR-020 screen 9) adds `GET /api/savings/kpis` (getSavingsKpis) and the GET half of `/api/savings` (getSavingsOpportunities) -- the fifth web epic to extend this document (task E07/F01/US01/T01 was the first, E07/F02/US01/T01 the second, E07/F03/US01/T01 the third, E08/F01/US01/T01 the fourth; see this paragraph's own 'repeating chore' provenance note above). Both operations were already named in this document's own provenance paragraph's backend-routes list ('GET/PATCH /api/savings and GET /api/savings/kpis') as not yet documented here; this task closes the GET half of that gap (already implemented by backend tasks E04/F02/US02/T01, E04/F03/US01/T01, E04/F03/US01/T02), it does not add new backend behaviour. `PATCH /api/savings/{id}` stays undocumented -- no screen in this task's own AC needs it (Home is read-only), so it is left for whichever future task first builds a real caller, the same 'wiring lands with the first real caller' convention this codebase already follows elsewhere. `confidenceLevel`/`status` are real, closed enums (SavingsConfidenceLevel.ToString() / SavingsOpportunityStatus.ToString()) declared with `enum`, the same way GET /api/renewals's own `status` field already is; `getSavingsKpis` never calls Raffa.Benchmark directly (it only aggregates Documents/Contracts and Savings data already at rest), so the Home screen's own 'benchmark provider unreachable' state (screens.md #9) is this call failing for any reason, not a status this endpoint reserves for that specific cause.

This task also found src/api/generated/schema.ts (the committed, supposedly-generated file `npm run generate:api` regenerates from this document) missing the closing brace for its top-level `operations` interface -- a pre-existing defect unrelated to this task's own two new operations, left by an earlier task that could not run the generator in this same harness (no `node`/`npm` on PATH; see AGENTS/CLAUDE instructions) and hand-appended its own operation block without re-closing the interface. Fixed in the same pass as this task's own additions rather than left to break every later task's `tsc --noEmit`.

Task E13/F09/US01/T03 (web-documents-v2, epic-13/feature-09 phase-3) adds `GET /api/documents` (listDocuments), `GET /api/documents/{id}/preview` (getDocumentPreview), `POST /api/documents/{id}/reprocess` (reprocessDocument), `DELETE /api/documents/{id}` (deleteDocument), the 413/415/422 responses on `POST /api/documents`, and widens `documentType` (Quote, Invoice, PriceList, Nda, Dpa alongside the original Msa/OrderForm/Sow/Amendment/RenewalLetter/Other) on every operation that already declared it. This task's own wave-spec `depends_on: [documents-v2-api, web-shell-v2]` -- the backend counterpart (epic-13/feature-04, tasks E13/F04/US01/T01 documents-admission and E13/F04/US01/T02 documents-v2-api) had not actually landed in this worktree when this task ran (checked: no `Documents:AdmissionThreshold`/`DocumentsEndpointExtensions.cs`/`DocumentAdmissionGate`/reprocess-or-preview-or-delete endpoint exists anywhere under `backend/` as of this commit, despite both backend tasks' own workitem files claiming exactly this surface). Rather than halt the whole web phase on an unmet upstream dependency this task cannot itself close, this document is authored directly from `inputs/requirements.md` §5.1/§6 (the named authoritative source both this task's own text and task-02-documents-v2-api.md's own text point to: "the phase-3 web task documents these endpoints from inputs/requirements.md §6") plus the two backend tasks' own workitem files for field names/algorithms neither requirements.md nor an ADR pins exactly (e.g. `DocumentProcessingSummary`'s real field set for the reprocess response, `ISupplierNameLookup`'s nullability for `supplierName`). Every new operation's own `description` above names this provenance individually. Widening the `documentType` enum is scoped to the Documents-only operations above (`listDocuments`, `getDocument`, `reprocessDocument`'s response) -- `getPortfolio`'s `items[].type` and `getContract360`'s `header.type`/`tabs.documents[].documentType` keep the original 6-member set, since Portfolio and Contract 360 are outside this task's own screens and widening their enums without also updating those already-shipped screens' own exhaustive-looking switches would be an uncalled-for, untested ripple; a future task that gives Portfolio/Contract 360 the same widened vocabulary can do so deliberately. When the backend tasks above do land, whichever lands last should diff its own real response shapes against this document rather than assume a silent match.

Task E13/F09/US01/T04 (web-ask-v2, epic-13/feature-09 phase-4) adds `GET/POST /api/conversations`, `GET /api/conversations/{id}`, `POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages` (the ADR-024 §6 reply contract), `GET /api/capabilities`, `GET /api/market/records/{id}` -- the sixth web epic to extend this document (see this paragraph's own 'repeating chore' provenance note above) -- plus `GET /api/insights/criticality` and `GET /api/contracts/{id}/strategy` (documented for completeness, no client.ts wrapper; see each operation's own description), and a `supplierName` property on getPortfolio's / getContract360's / getRenewals' response items (R-SUP-04; already real on listDocuments since task E13/F09/US01/T03). Every new operation's own description names its exact provenance; two are worth flagging here: `GET /api/market/records/{id}`'s real backend handler (backend/src/Raffa.Api/MarketEndpointExtensions.cs) does not compile as of this commit (two concatenated method bodies, confirmed by reading the file directly), so this operation is authored from the clean domain types underneath it, not the broken handler; and the existing `askRaffa` operation below (`POST /api/chat/query`) still documents the pre-ADR-024 `{question,intent,canDetermine,answer,citations,message}` shape that ChatEndpointExtensions.cs's own doc comment says was 'replaced entirely' -- left untouched here since this task's own web screens (web/src/routes/ask/**) no longer call it at all, replaced by the conversations endpoints above; a future task that removes the V1 alias and its stale documentation together can close that gap.

Task E18/F02/US02/T01 (wave w16, NW-08; story us-02-audit-read-for-a-real-admin) adds `GET /api/audit` -- closing the gap this document's own provenance paragraph above named ('GET /api/audit' is removed from that not-yet-documented list, since the route is documented from this task on). Already implemented by backend task E01/F06/US02/T02, and reachable by a real caller only from this task on: it swaps the route's guard from a claims-based check (`WorkspacePrincipalAuthorization`, unreachable by any real client, deleted whole by this task) to the same `ICallerContext`/`WorkspaceRoleResolver` membership ladder `POST /api/documents/{id}/reprocess` and `DELETE /api/documents/{id}` already use (ADR-025 §K). `X-Tenant-Id` is declared as a required header for the first time on this route (ADR-026 w16 clause 2: 'a route that gains a required header silently is a runtime discovery'), even though it is documentation `tsc` cannot check -- the generator parses only `responses` (see this file's own 'Codegen tool choice' paragraph above). No `client.ts` wrapper: this route has no caller in any shipped web screen (product-owner ruled no web audit surface in scope, OQ-w16-003), so it joins the documented-but-unwrapped set `GET /api/insights/criticality` and `GET /api/contracts/{id}/strategy` already establish (ADR-012 w16 footer clauses 24, 27) -- the generated schema.ts type, arriving at zero extra cost when schema.ts is regenerated wholesale, is what this story's client-side acceptance is satisfied by.

Task E19/F06/US01/T01 (wave w16, theme B contract+client) adds GET `/api/renewals/{id}/action`, `savedAction` on GET `/api/renewals` items, GET `/api/quotes`, GET `/api/quotes/{id}` (outcomes newest first), and GET/PUT `/api/contracts/{id}/negotiation-steps`. Wrappers in client.ts are only `getQuote`, `getNegotiationSteps`, `putNegotiationSteps`. GET `/api/renewals/{id}/action` and GET `/api/quotes` are published unwrapped on purpose (same set as `/api/insights/criticality` and GET `/api/contracts/{id}/strategy`): screens reach the action via `savedAction` on `getRenewals`, and no shipped screen lists quotes.

servers.description: Relative to the runtime-configured API origin (AppConfig.apiBaseUrl, ADR-012 "config, not code"; see web/src/config/appConfig.ts). This document intentionally does not hard-code a dev/demo host.

get.summary: Liveness/readiness probe.
get.description: Maps 1:1 to `app.MapHealthChecks("/health")` in backend/src/Raffa.Api/Program.cs, which registers no custom HealthCheckOptions.ResponseWriter -- so it uses ASP.NET Core's default plain-text writer (Content-Type: text/plain, body is just the status name) rather than a JSON body. The 200-on-healthy case is verified by backend/tests/Raffa.Api.Tests/DeployableApiTests.cs (Health_endpoint_returns_200_ok); the Degraded/Unhealthy cases follow Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks' documented default status-code mapping (Healthy/Degraded -> 200, Unhealthy -> 503), which this repo has not overridden.

200.description: Healthy or Degraded.

get.summary: List the workspaces the caller belongs to.
get.description: Maps to the new ListWorkspacesAsync handler in backend/src/Raffa.Api/WorkspaceEndpointExtensions.cs (task E14/F03/US01/T01, wave w14 'workspace is real'; ADR-026 section D1, ADR-025 sections F.1/F.3), backed by the new WorkspaceDirectoryService.ListForIdentityAsync (backend/src/Raffa.Identity.Workspace/Infrastructure/WorkspaceDirectoryService.cs) joined in the host with PortfolioQueryService.CountValidatedContractsAsync (backend/src/Raffa.Documents.Contracts/Application/PortfolioQueryService.cs). Takes no tenant header of any kind, ever (acceptance N5) -- the response is derived exclusively from the caller identity's own live workspace_membership rows. Empty list is 200 + [], never 404; ordered by createdAt ascending, stable. contractCount is the validated-contract count (at least one linked document reaching ProcessingStatus.Completed -- the same definition already served as contractsAnalyzedCount on GET /api/savings/kpis, ADR-026 section D2); country/currency are the workspace's own profile columns (NW-24, ADR-003 w14 footer), absent when never set, never a fabricated default. role is a plain string, never an enum (ADR-026 Amendment #3 -- workspace_role.name is a per-tenant row, not a closed set the client can validate against); there is deliberately no roleLabel property -- the picker derives its own tag from role.

parameters.name: X-User-Id
parameters.description: The caller's interim identity (ADR-022, ADR-025 section A). Absent or blank -> 401. Confers no role, no tenant and no scope -- only which workspace_user rows to discover.

200.description: Every workspace the caller holds a live workspace_membership in, oldest first, plus any tenant where they hold a live invitation but no membership yet. A caller who belongs to nothing gets 200 with both arrays empty, never 404.

role.description: The caller's own highest role in this workspace. A plain string, never an enum -- see this operation's own description.

contractCount.description: Validated contracts only (>= 1 linked document Completed) -- the same fact contractsAnalyzedCount already serves elsewhere.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or null when never set (NW-24).

currency.description: ISO 4217 alpha-3, derived from country and stored -- or null when country was never set. Never a fabricated default.

pendingInvitations.description: Fix 2026-09-14 (WorkspaceDirectoryService.DiscoverForIdentityAsync). Normally empty -- a tenant appears here only when this identity holds no live membership but does hold a live (unaccepted, unrevoked, unexpired) invitation, most often because the token-bearing /invite/accept flow never completed. Never a trust: acceptInvitationForIdentity (POST /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/invites/accept) re-verifies liveness from scratch before granting anything.

role.description: The offered role. A plain string, never an enum (ADR-026 Amendment #3).

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 section B.

post.description: Maps 1:1 to CreateWorkspaceAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/WorkspaceEndpointExtensions.cs (task E01/F09/US01/T01, r0-integration). Task E14/F02/US01/T01 (wave w14) made a presented identity required (X-User-Id via the ICallerIdentity seam; absent or blank -> 401, ADR-025 section B) and made the creator that identity's own Admin membership, unconditionally -- a role property does not exist on this request body and is never honoured (ADR-025 Rule D.2b). Task E14/F03/US01/T01 (wave w14) adds industry/country to the body (NW-24): currency is derived from country and stored, never typed; country must be one of CH/IT/DE/AT (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, ADR-003 w14 footer) or omitted entirely; an unsupported country is a 400 through the existing Result<T> failure path, never a raw Postgres length error; a value never supplied is stored and returned absent, never an invented 'CHF'. The 201 body's own role property (added by E14/F02/US01/T01) lets the SPA enter the new workspace without a second call. GET /api/workspaces (also added by task E14/F03/US01/T01) is the list-workspaces-for-caller endpoint this description used to say did not exist yet.

name.description: Workspace display name. WorkspaceProvisioningService.CreateWorkspaceAsync trims it and fails (400) if blank.

industry.description: Optional free text (NW-24; a closed list at the UI, not re-validated server-side beyond a 120-character bound). Trimmed; blank is stored as absent.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, one of CH/IT/DE/AT (ADR-003 w14 footer). Anything else -> 400. Drives the derived, stored currency (CH -> CHF, IT/DE/AT -> EUR).

201.description: Workspace created; the caller is its Admin.

id.description: WorkspaceTenant.TenantId.Value (a Guid) -- also the workspace row's own Id (WorkspaceTenant's `Id == TenantId` invariant).

role.description: Always "Admin" -- the creator's own role, unconditionally (ADR-025 Rule D.2b). A plain string, never an enum (ADR-026 Amendment #3).

400.description: Blank name, an unsupported country, or another validation failure surfaced via WorkspaceProvisioningService.CreateWorkspaceAsync's Result<T>.Error (a plain string, serialized as a JSON string body by Results.BadRequest).

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 section B.

get.summary: The roster of a workspace: live members plus pending invitations.
get.description: Documents the ADR-026 section D3 contract (verbatim, per its own w14 footer clause 1) for the E14/F04/US01/T01 handler in backend/src/Raffa.Api/WorkspaceMembersEndpointExtensions.cs -- a same-phase sibling task's file; this task (E14/F03/US01/T01) only documents the contract and writes the client method. Only X-User-Id is sent, never X-Tenant-Id: the route's {tenantId} already carries the tenant and the caller's membership in it is verified (ADR-026's own w14 footer supersedes its earlier D3 header line -- two accepted ADRs cannot carry opposite instructions for one operation, and ADR-022's w14 footer is the general rule). The roster is live workspace_membership rows union live (unaccepted, unrevoked, unexpired) workspace_invitation rows -- never a scan of workspace_user, so a removed member never reappears. status is derived, never stored: Active for a live membership, Invited for a live invitation with no membership yet. name maps to the existing nullable WorkspaceUser.DisplayName, emitted only when a real stored value exists -- never derived from the email address. role and status are plain strings, never enums (ADR-026 Amendment #3 -- the same generator/schema reasoning as listWorkspaces' own role field). 2026-09-11 fix (the gap E15/F02/US01/T01 halted on): membershipId and invitationId are the action ids -- exactly one is present per row, matching status (Active -> membershipId, the id DELETE /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/members/{membershipId} takes; Invited -> invitationId, the id DELETE /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/invites/{id} takes). id alone (WorkspaceUser's, stable across the Active/Invited transition) cannot address either action.

parameters.name: X-User-Id
parameters.description: The caller's interim identity (ADR-022, ADR-025 section A). Absent or blank -> 401. The route already carries the tenant -- this is not X-Tenant-Id and no such header is accepted here.

200.description: Any live member of the tenant may read the roster (ADR-025 Rule D.4a) -- Procurement included, read-only.

name.description: WorkspaceUser.DisplayName, or null -- never derived from email.

status.description: "Active" (a live membership) or "Invited" (a live invitation, no membership yet) -- derived, never stored (ADR-026 section D3).

membershipId.description: Set only when status is "Active" -- the id DELETE /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/members/{membershipId} takes. Never id (WorkspaceUser's own id).

invitationId.description: Set only when status is "Invited" -- the id DELETE /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/invites/{id} takes.

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 section B.

404.description: Caller is not a live member of this tenant (ADR-025 Rule D.4b -- never 403 for a non-member, and never an empty 200).

delete.summary: Remove a member from a workspace (Admin only), with the last-Admin guard.
delete.description: Task E15/F01/US01/T01 (wave w14; ADR-025 Rule D.5a-c, AC-7/AC-9). Deletes the workspace_membership row (never the workspace_user row -- audit continuity) and revokes that person's unaccepted invitations in this tenant in the same transaction (AC-8's own 're-adding needs a new invite' would otherwise be false). Immediate: nothing caches authorization, so the removed identity's very next request in this tenant already reflects it. The last-Admin guard is a pure domain function (WorkspaceMembershipRemoval.CanRemove) -- removing the sole Admin (including removing yourself) is refused with 409, never a 500 or a silent no-op.

parameters.name: membershipId
parameters.description: WorkspaceMembership.Id, as returned by getWorkspaceMembers' own roster rows (member.id).

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 §B.

403.description: Caller is a live member of this tenant, but not Admin.

404.description: Caller is not a live member of this tenant (never 403 for a non-member, ADR-025 Rule B1); or the membership id does not exist in this tenant.

409.description: The target membership is the tenant's sole live Admin -- at least one must always remain (ADR-025 Rule D.5a). Applies whether the caller is removing themselves or another Admin.

post.summary: Invite a member into a workspace with a role.
post.description: Maps to WorkspaceEndpointExtensions.InviteAsync (task E01/F09/US01/T01). The target tenant comes from the route, not a caller claim (ADR-010/Entra ID is not wired into this host yet) -- no X-Tenant-Id header here either, for the same reason.

201.description: An invitation was issued (task E15/F01/US01/T01, wave w14; ADR-025 §D.1, ADR-026 §D5). This is an offer, not a grant: no workspace_membership row is written until the invitee calls POST /api/invites/accept. Since task E17/F01/US01/T01 (wave w15, NW-67/NW-68; ADR-026 w15 footers §1/§4/§8, ADR-025 §J): the guest was provisioned in the company directory BEFORE this row was written (a provisioning failure is the 502 below, never a 201); acceptUrl is absolute ({Invitations__AcceptUrlBase}/invite/accept#<token>) when a base is configured and site-relative otherwise -- the token stays after the `#` (ADR-025 Rule C9) and appears in this response exactly once; the mail, when a transport is configured, is the second channel for the same link. `deliveryOutcome` is the one discriminant the pane branches on; `mailDelivered` stays what it always was (the mailer's own bool, accepted for delivery, never a receipt) and `deliveryOutcome == "sent"` if and only if `mailDelivered`. A live invitation for the same address is REPLACED by this call (revoked and re-issued in one transaction), so the link the Admin already shared stops working.

id.description: The invitation's own id -- also the {id} DELETE /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/invites/{id} (revoke) takes.

expiresAt.description: 7 days from issue, absolute (ADR-025 Rule C7).

acceptUrl.description: Site-relative /invite/accept#<token> -- a URL fragment, never a path or query string (ADR-025 Rule C9).

deliveryOutcome.description: ADR-026 w15 footer §8: the server's own delivery discriminant -- `sent` (the mail was accepted for delivery), `mail_failed` (a transport is configured and refused; the copyable acceptUrl is the remedy), `no_transport` (no mail transport is configured; the copyable acceptUrl is the only channel). Non-nullable with an enum on purpose (ADR-012 w15 §9): the generator renders a literal union, which is what keeps the pane's three-arm branch exhaustive under tsc. There is no fourth value -- a guest-provisioning failure is the 502 below, not a 201.

mailDelivered.description: IInvitationMailer.TrySendAsync's own return: accepted for delivery, never a delivery receipt (ADR-025 §J.6e). Equals `deliveryOutcome == "sent"` by construction; the client branches on `deliveryOutcome` and never combines the two.

identityProvisioned.description: ADR-026 w15 footer §1: true when the company directory holds a guest for this address after the call -- created by it or already present, deliberately indistinguishable (ADR-025 §J.4a, no directory-enumeration oracle) -- and false when guest provisioning is not configured (Invitations__GuestProvisioning__Enabled). `false` means NOT CONFIGURED, never failed: a failure is the 502 below. The pane keys the one-time-code sentence to this boolean.

400.description: Missing/invalid route tenantId, blank email, unrecognized role, or a validation failure surfaced via WorkspaceMembershipService.InviteAsync's own outcome.

409.description: This email already holds that role in this workspace (a live MEMBERSHIP is never re-issued), the workspace has reached its cap of live invitations (100 distinct addresses, ADR-025 §J.1c.4), or two concurrent invites for one address raced ADR-026 §D4's partial unique index. Since task E17/F01/US01/T01 (ADR-025 §J.2b) a live (unaccepted, unrevoked) invitation is NOT a 409 any more: it is replaced by the new one in one transaction. A removed person (no live membership, and their prior invitation revoked by the removal itself) is not blocked by this -- see DELETE /api/workspaces/{tenantId}/members/{membershipId}.

502.description: Task E17/F01/US01/T01 (wave w15; ADR-026 w15 footer §3, ADR-025 §J.2a/§J.4): the company directory did not provision a guest for this address, so the invitation was ABORTED -- no invitation row, no token, no mail; the address slot is free and the Admin may retry at once. `failureReason` is a closed set the pane maps onto ADR-020 w15 §3.5's copy (and a catch-all row for any value outside it); the directory's own error body is never surfaced (§J.4b). Declared inline, non-nullable, with an enum, so the generated client types it and the pane never string-matches server prose (ADR-012 w15 §13.2).

failureReason.description: `consent_missing`: the directory answered 401/403 -- the User.Invite.All application permission is not consented or a directory policy forbids invitations. `provisioning_failed`: the directory refused this request (an address it will not add, a refused domain). `directory_unavailable`: the directory could not be reached or failed on its side.

delete.description: Task E15/F01/US01/T01 (wave w14; ADR-025 Rule D.5, AC-11). Stamps revoked_at; the accept link stops working on the very next request -- nothing caches it. Same identity -> membership -> Admin guard as POST .../invites (401 -> 404 non-member -> 403 non-Admin -> 204).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: WorkspaceInvitation.Id, as returned by inviteWorkspaceMember's own 201 body.

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 §B.

403.description: Caller is a live member of this tenant, but not Admin.

404.description: Caller is not a live member of this tenant (never 403 for a non-member, ADR-025 Rule B1); or the invitation id does not exist, or is already accepted/revoked, in this tenant.

post.summary: Accept a live invitation for the signed-in identity, no token required.
post.description: Fix 2026-09-14. The identity-keyed counterpart of acceptInvitation (POST /api/invites/accept): extends ADR-025 §F.3 Exception 2 with a second entry point into the same already-sanctioned shape -- still one tenant, still no membership check (the caller is not a member yet, by definition), still a same-request re-verification before any write, only the evidence changes from 'possession of the 256-bit secret' to 'a live invitation whose email belongs to this signed-in identity'. Exists because the token-bearing accept screen (/invite/accept) must complete inside one browser tab/popup with no page navigation (ADR-025 Rule C10 forbids persisting the token to any browser storage) -- fragile in practice, since a blocked or non-closing loginPopup strands the invitee signed in with no memory of the invitation. The tenantId this runs against always comes from the same identity's own prior GET /api/workspaces call, which surfaces it under pendingInvitations; this endpoint trusts that provenance no more than acceptInvitation trusts a token's tenant prefix -- both re-verify from scratch before granting anything. No body. Deliberately no 409: there is no token to re-present after success, so a second call simply finds no live invitation left and answers 404, not a new outcome to design for.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant a prior GET /api/workspaces surfaced under pendingInvitations[].tenantId -- re-verified from scratch, never trusted as a grant.

parameters.name: X-User-Id
parameters.description: The caller's interim identity (ADR-022, ADR-025 §A). Absent or blank -> 401.

200.description: Accepted: the caller now holds a live membership at the invited role -- the identical shape acceptInvitation's own 200 returns.

role.description: The invited role, now granted. A plain string, never an enum (ADR-026 Amendment #3).

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 §B.

404.description: No live invitation matches this identity in this tenant -- an unrelated tenant and 'not actually invited' collapse to the same answer (Rule B1).

410.description: A live invitation matched, but it has expired.

get.summary: Pre-accept: read what an invitation offers, without accepting it.
get.description: Task E15/F01/US01/T01 (wave w14; ADR-025 Rule D.3e/C4/C5, ADR-026 §D5). Not parameterised on {token} -- the token travels in the X-Invitation-Token header, never a path or query string (ADR-025 Rule C9: a query string lands in access logs, Referer headers and browser history). Returns workspace name, offered role and expiry, and nothing else, ever -- not the invited email (echoing it turns a leaked link into an address-discovery tool), no roster, no counts. A token holder is not yet a member.

parameters.name: X-Invitation-Token
parameters.description: {tenantId:N}.{secret} (ADR-025 §C). Absent/blank/malformed -> 404, with no tenant scope ever entered (Rule C4).

200.description: A live (unaccepted, unrevoked, unexpired) invitation matched the token.

role.description: The role this invitation offers. A plain string, never an enum (ADR-026 Amendment #3).

404.description: Token absent, malformed, unknown, revoked, or already accepted -- one indistinguishable answer for every 'not yours' case (ADR-025 §B).

410.description: The token is well-formed and matches a real invitation, but it has expired (ADR-025 §B) -- the one disclosure worth making, safe only because reaching this branch already proves possession of the 256-bit secret.

post.summary: Accept an invitation: bind the signed-in identity and grant the membership.
post.description: Task E15/F01/US01/T01 (wave w14; ADR-025 Rule D.3a-d, ADR-026 §D5). Not parameterised on {token} -- same X-Invitation-Token header as getInvitation (ADR-025 Rule C9). Requires a presented identity (X-User-Id; absent -> 401 -- there would otherwise be no subject to bind). On success, in one transaction: binds the accepting identity's external subject onto the workspace_user row the invite already wrote, inserts the membership at the invited role, and stamps accepted_at. The signed-in identity's email must match the invited address case-insensitively, or 403 with a reason that never echoes the invited address (Rule D.3b). A second accept by the same identity is 409 (idempotency signal); by two concurrent callers, exactly one membership row and one 409, never a 500 (the unique index ix_workspace_membership_workspace_user_id_workspace_role_id already enforces the row -- this only translates the violation).

parameters.name: X-Invitation-Token
parameters.description: {tenantId:N}.{secret} (ADR-025 §C). Absent/blank/malformed -> 404, with no tenant scope ever entered (Rule C4).

parameters.name: X-User-Id
parameters.description: The caller's interim identity (ADR-022, ADR-025 §A). Absent or blank -> 401.

200.description: Accepted: the caller now holds a live membership at the invited role.

role.description: The invited role, now granted. A plain string, never an enum (ADR-026 Amendment #3).

401.description: No identity presented (X-User-Id absent or blank) -- ADR-025 §B.

403.description: The signed-in identity's email does not match the invited address. The reason never echoes the invited address (Rule D.3b).

404.description: Token absent, malformed, unknown, or revoked; or already accepted by a different identity -- one indistinguishable answer for every 'not yours' case (ADR-025 §B).

409.description: Already accepted by this same identity (idempotency signal), or two concurrent accepts raced the same unique index -- translated here, never a 500.

410.description: The token is well-formed and matches a real invitation, but it has expired.

post.summary: Upload a document; stored at once, processed by the Worker afterwards.
post.description: Maps to Raffa.Api.DocumentsEndpointExtensions.UploadDocumentAsync. Task E16/F02/US03/T01 (ADR-027 §D1): the request returns as soon as the bytes are durable in blob storage and a `document` row plus a queued `extraction_job` exist -- no parse, no classification and no AI-gateway call happen on the request path any more. The Worker (Raffa.Worker, ADR-027 §D2/§D3) claims the job from the durable queue and runs admission + the parse -> classify -> extract pipeline; poll `GET /api/documents/{id}` or `GET /api/documents` to watch `processingStatus` move from `Uploaded` to `Processing` and then to a terminal value (`Completed`, `NeedsReview`, `Failed`, or `Rejected` with a `rejectionReason`). Size (413) and format (415) are still refused on the request path -- they need no AI. Interim X-Tenant-Id header placeholder pending ADR-010 claim-based tenant resolution.

201.description: Stored and queued (ADR-027 §D1). `contractId` is always null here: no contract exists until the Worker has classified and extracted the document. `processingStatus` is always `Uploaded` at this point; the wider enum is the same one every other document surface uses. `mimeType` is the sniffed canonical type (`application/pdf`, the two OOXML types, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`), never the browser's declared `Content-Type`.

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id header, a non-multipart body, an empty/missing 'file' field, or DocumentUploadService.UploadAsync's Result.Error.

413.description: Task E13/F04/US01/T01 (documents-admission): file exceeds `Documents:MaxFileBytes` (50 MB), rejected before any parse or AI-gateway call -- both the declared `Content-Length` and the received part are checked (`Raffa.Api.DocumentsEndpointExtensions`). Plain-string body, same `Results.Json(string)` shape as the 415 below and the 400 above.

application/json.example: Raffa accepts files up to 50 MB. This file is larger.

415.description: Task E13/F04/US01/T01: format rejected by extension **and** magic-byte sniffing (`Raffa.Documents.Contracts.Application.Admission.DocumentFormatSniffer`) before any parse or AI-gateway call -- a `.zip` renamed `.pdf` lands here, never a 422 (R-DOC-02 AC-1), and so does a PNG renamed `.pdf`. Accepted: `.pdf` (`%PDF-` header), `.docx`/`.xlsx` (OOXML package holding `word/document.xml` / `xl/workbook.xml`), `.png`, `.jpg`/`.jpeg`. Plain-string body, quoted verbatim from `inputs/requirements.md` R-DOC-02.

application/json.example: Raffa reads PDF, Word, Excel and scanned images

422.description: Retired by task E16/F02/US03/T01 (ADR-027 §D6): the admission gate now runs in the Worker, after the upload has returned, so a document classified as `Other` (or with no readable text) is stored first and then marked `processingStatus: Rejected` with a `rejectionReason` on `GET /api/documents` / `GET /api/documents/{id}`; its blob is deleted at that point. Kept in the document only so older clients' typings still compile; the upload endpoint no longer emits it.

confidence.description: The classify role's own confidence, 0-1. Always present, even for `no_readable_text` (0 -- classify never ran; see DocumentAdmissionGate).

hint.example: Raffa only keeps contracts, order forms, quotes and the documents around them.

get.summary: List the tenant's documents (server-side, survives a reload).
get.description: Task E13/F09/US01/T03 (web-documents-v2), documenting `inputs/requirements.md` R-DOC-06/R-DOC-09/§6 and `Raffa.Documents.Contracts.Application.DocumentQueryService.ListAsync`'s own planned shape (task-02-documents-v2-api.md point 3) ahead of that backend task actually landing in this worktree -- see this document's own top-level provenance note. Replaces the web's own `sessionStorage`-tracked list (`documentStore.ts`); AC-1 "reloading the browser shows the same list as before" depends on this call, not client storage. `status` filters to one exact `processingStatus` value when supplied (the same single-status convention `GET /api/contracts?status=` already uses) -- Documents V2's own "Needs your attention" vs "All documents" toggle is **not** this parameter (attention is a union of three statuses); the web client fetches the tenant's whole list unfiltered and buckets client-side (`documentsListViewModel.ts`), the same fetch-once/filter-local architecture `GET /api/contracts` already established for Portfolio.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Exact match on Document.ProcessingStatus (`Rejected` included since task E16/F02/US03/T01, ADR-027 §D6). Omit to return every status (the web client's own default read).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Defaults to 25; same 100-row ceiling convention `GET /api/contracts` already documents.

200.description: Tenant-scoped document list, newest-created-first.

supplierName.description: Resolved via `ISupplierNameLookup` (F03/T01, same phase) when registered; null otherwise -- never a raw supplier id.

stage.description: R-DOC-09's real stage name (`Uploading` | `Classifying` | `OCR / text` | `Sections & tables` | `Extracting facts` | `Validating schema`), present only while `processingStatus` is `Processing`; null once terminal (or before processing has started). Not declared with `enum` alongside the nullable union -- see this document's own `getPortfolio` operation for why (generate-api-client.mjs#renderSchemaType drops the null member when both are combined).

pageCount.description: Null until the hybrid parse stage has run at least once.

weakFactCount.description: Fields below the review threshold (spec §7.3), 0 once validated or for a document with none. Drives the row action's real "Review N fields" count (screens-v2.md #3).

rejectionReason.description: ADR-027 §D6: `not_a_contract` or `no_readable_text` while `processingStatus` is `Rejected` (the same reason codes ADR-024's retired 422 body carried); null for every other status. Not declared with `enum` alongside the nullable union -- same generator limitation this document's `stage` property documents.

errorDetail.description: Latest extraction-job error while `processingStatus` is `Failed`; null otherwise. The Documents list surfaces this instead of only 'Not yet linked to a contract'.

counts.description: ADR-027 §D7 with §C5/§C9: tenant-wide, independent of `status`/`page` -- the same five numbers whichever page or filter was requested, so the rail badge, the segmented toggle and the summary line never disagree with the list. Five overlapping projections of one grouped query, never a partition: `needsAttention` (not `Completed`, not `Rejected`) contains `processing` (`Uploaded` + `Processing`), and `needsReview` sits inside both; `rejected` sits outside `all` altogether (a rejected file was never added). No sum holds, every surface reads exactly one member, and a client must not derive "askable" from `all - needsAttention` -- askability is the contract-level number `GET /api/workspaces` already carries.

all.description: Every document of the tenant except the `Rejected` ones -- the "All documents · N" number, which is what makes "never counted" a server fact.

needsAttention.description: Documents that are not `Completed` and not `Rejected` -- `Uploaded` + `Processing` + `NeedsReview` + `Failed` (ADR-027 §C9): exactly the set the web's own "Needs your attention" filter lists, computed once on the server so the chip's number and the rows it filters to are the same set. Contains `processing`.

needsReview.description: Documents in `NeedsReview` alone (ADR-027 §C5) -- the "K waiting for your review" number; inside both `all` and `needsAttention`.

processing.description: Documents in `Uploaded` or `Processing` -- still moving through the Worker.

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id header, or a malformed status/page query parameter.

get.summary: Read back one document's metadata and processing status.
get.description: Maps to the inline handler in Program.cs (task E01/F06/US01/T02). Same interim X-Tenant-Id header placeholder as POST /api/documents. Task E13/F04/US01/T01 widens `documentType` below (5 new admitted types beyond the original 6-member set; existing names unchanged) -- see the `/api/documents` GET (`listDocuments`) operation above for the same widened set and its own provenance note.

200.description: Document found for this tenant.

pageCount.description: Persisted document.page_count; null until the Worker has parsed the file. 1-based page count the viewer uses with GET /api/documents/{id}/preview?page=n.

isPageCountLimited.description: True when pageCount exceeds the OCR budget and only MaxPagesPerDocument pages were rendered.

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id header, or a non-GUID id in the route.

404.description: No such document for this tenant.

delete.summary: Delete a document (Admin only): blob, preview, row, embeddings; detaches the contract link.
delete.description: Task E13/F04/US01/T02 (documents-v2-api), documented ahead of that backend task landing in this worktree -- see this document's own top-level provenance note; shape from `inputs/requirements.md` R-DOC-10/§6. Audits `document.deleted`. Admin-only: a live workspace_membership row for the caller's validated identity (WorkspaceRoleResolver). Missing/non-GUID X-Tenant-Id -> 400; a well-formed tenant with no live membership -> 404; a live member who is not Admin -> 403.

403.description: Caller is not Admin (Procurement gets 403, R-DOC-10).

404.description: No such document for this tenant.

get.summary: Page preview PNG (or an honest placeholder for DOCX/XLSX), tenant-scoped.
get.description: Task E13/F04/US01/T02, documented ahead of that backend task landing in this worktree -- see this document's own top-level provenance note; shape from `inputs/requirements.md` R-DOC-08/§6. Always `image/png` on 200 regardless of source document type (ADR-009 "never a raw blob URL" -- always proxied through this endpoint, never a Storage URL). Optional 1-based `page` query (NW-26 / E22/F02): absent means page 1; out of range is 404. The web client (`getDocumentPreviewUrl`) fetches this with the `X-Tenant-Id` header (a plain `` cannot carry a custom header) and turns the response into a browser object URL -- see `src/api/client.ts`'s own doc comment on that method.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page to rasterise. Absent means page 1. Out of range is 404, never a silent page 1.

200.description: PNG of page 1 (PDF/images) or a generated placeholder (DOCX/XLSX).

404.description: No such document for this tenant.

post.summary: Queue a re-run of hybrid parse + embedding (Admin only) so retrieval never cites raw bytes.
post.description: Maps to Raffa.Api.DocumentsEndpointExtensions' reprocess handler backed by `Raffa.Documents.Contracts.Application.DocumentReprocessService`. Task E16/F02/US03/T01 (ADR-027 §D1): the old page-aware chunks are dropped, the document goes back to `Uploaded`, a fresh classification `extraction_job` is queued and the request returns 202 with `{documentId, extractionJobId, processingStatus}` -- the Worker does the re-parse/re-embed afterwards, exactly like a first upload. Poll `GET /api/documents/{id}` for the terminal status; every new embedding row carries a page number (R-DOC-07 AC-2). Admin-only via membership, same ladder as `deleteDocument`.

extractionJobId.description: The queued classification job the Worker will claim (ADR-027 §D3).

processingStatus.description: Always `Uploaded` at this point; the wider enum is the one every other document surface uses.

404.description: No such document for this tenant.

post.summary: Ask the Worker to take this still-queued document at its next free slot, ahead of the FIFO (task E16/F03/US02/T01, ADR-027 w15 footer C12).
post.description: Maps to Raffa.Api.DocumentsEndpointExtensions' prioritise handler backed by `Raffa.Documents.Contracts.Application.DocumentPriorityService`. The web calls it once when a user opens a document whose row is still `Uploaded`/`Processing`: the document's queued, unclaimed classification job is stamped `prioritised_at`, and the next delivery any Worker replica handles in this tenant runs that job before its own. Any live member may call it; it grants nothing but an order. 204 whenever the document exists -- already claimed, already prioritised or already terminal are no-ops, so the client may call it blindly. Poll `GET /api/documents` for the stage.

204.description: The request was recorded (or there was nothing left to prioritise). Poll the list for the stage.

400.description: The document id in the route is not a GUID, or the tenant header is missing/malformed.

404.description: No such document for this tenant, or the caller is not a member of it (never 403, ADR-025 Rule B1).

post.summary: Review sign-off: mark a reviewed document validated (needs_review -> completed).
post.description: Maps to ValidateDocumentAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/DocumentsEndpointExtensions.cs, backed by Raffa.Documents.Contracts.Application.DocumentValidationService. The one write behind the review screen's "Mark as validated" (ADR-020 screen 6; product spec §7.1 "needs review -> completed", §7.3 human-in-the-loop): field corrections are already durable through PATCH /api/contracts/{id}, so this call records the reviewer's sign-off as the document's status plus one `document.validated` audit row naming the accepted fields. It never rewrites the extraction evidence (Appendix C rule 5). Not Admin-only: reviewing is the Procurement role's own job, same posture as PATCH /api/contracts/{id}. Idempotent -- validating an already completed document answers 200 with `alreadyValidated: true`. Same interim X-Tenant-Id / X-User-Id header posture as every other operation here.

acceptedFields.description: Field names the reviewer accepted as extracted (ExtractionEvidence.FieldName / ContractCorrectionService.CorrectableFieldNames keys, e.g. currency, autoRenewal, supplier). Omit or send [] when every flagged field was corrected instead. Recorded on the audit row.

200.description: The document is now completed (or already was).

processingStatus.description: Always `Completed` on a 200; the enum is the shared DocumentProcessingStatus vocabulary.

acceptedFields.description: The request's acceptedFields, trimmed and de-duplicated -- what the audit row recorded.

alreadyValidated.description: True when the document was already Completed before this call (idempotent no-op, still audited).

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id header, or a non-GUID id in the route.

404.description: No such document for this tenant.

409.description: The document is not in a reviewable state: still Uploaded/Processing (nothing to sign off yet) or Failed (reprocess it first). The body is the named reason (DocumentValidationService.StillProcessingError / FailedProcessingError).

get.summary: List the tenant's contract portfolio (filters + paging).
get.description:
Maps to GetPortfolioAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/PortfolioEndpointExtensions.cs (task E02/F03/US01/T01 filters; T02 paging), backed by PortfolioQueryService.GetPortfolioAsync. Task E07/F01/US01/T01 (us-01-portfolio-list-filters) adds this operation -- the first web epic to build a screen against one of the E02-E05 backend routes this document's own provenance paragraph already named as outstanding. Same interim X-Tenant-Id header placeholder as every other operation above (ADR-010 is not wired into Program.cs yet).

The 200 response's risk field is deliberately typed below as a bare nullable string, not a nullable enum, even though the real wire values are exactly Low/Medium/High/Critical or null (RiskSeverity.ToString(), or null when a contract has no recorded risk row). web/scripts/generate-api-client.mjs#renderSchemaType checks a schema's enum before it checks whether type is an array -- every enum this document declared before this task was always non-nullable, so a schema combining both never came up, and the generator silently drops the null member when they are combined. Rather than patch the generator (outside this task's own file scope -- the portfolio screen, not the codegen tool), this operation's risk schema omits enum so the generator's existing, already-correct type-array branch produces the honest string-or-null TypeScript type; src/api/client.ts names the real four-value set as its own hand-written PortfolioRiskSeverity alias, with a runtime check at the one place a raw string crosses into it.

parameters.name: supplierId
parameters.description: Exact-match Contract.SupplierId (a bare cross-module id -- Suppliers/Products has no name to filter by yet).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Exact, case-sensitive match against Contract.Status -- a free-text field (bootstrap default is the literal string processing; otherwise whatever the metadata extraction stage last wrote), not a closed enum yet.

parameters.name: renewalFrom
parameters.description: Only ever matches an auto-renewing contract's EndDate -- PortfolioListItem.RenewalDate is null otherwise.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Exact-match Supplier.Category, resolved by a host join in PortfolioEndpointExtensions -- Raffa.Documents.Contracts cannot reference Raffa.Suppliers.Products (ADR-002), so PortfolioQueryService only carries this value past itself, never resolves it (task E24/F01/US01/T01, story us-01-portfolio-category-backend; closes NW-23/OQ-w17-007). Blank or absent leaves the full tenant-scoped portfolio; a category no supplier on the page carries -- including one that matches no supplier at all -- narrows to an empty items array, never a fabricated one.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Defaults to 25; PortfolioPageRequest.MaxPageSize caps it at 100.

200.description: Tenant-scoped portfolio page, newest-created-first, already risk-joined.

supplierName.description: The supplier's display name, resolved from `supplierId` through `ISupplierNameLookup` in one batched call per page -- never a raw supplier id (R-SUP-04, ADR-024). Null when the contract has no supplier, and also when the id no longer resolves for this tenant: the lookup port never fabricates a placeholder name, so a dangling link reads as an id with no name rather than silently losing both. Projected by PortfolioEndpointExtensions.GetPortfolioAsync (task E13/F03/US01/T02); the property was documented here one task earlier (E13/F09/US01/T04) while the backend still only carried the id.

currency.description: The contract's own ISO currency code (Contract.Currency). Added so the V2 Portfolio summary can sum annualSpend per currency ("N validated contracts · CHF 4.2M annual"); deliberately not in `required` so earlier typed fixtures stay valid -- the backend always emits it.

renewalDate.description: Equals endDate only when autoRenewal is true; otherwise null (PortfolioListItem.cs).

risk.description: Low, Medium, High, or Critical, or null when the contract has no recorded Risk row. Deliberately not declared as an enum here -- see this operation's own description for why.

fileName.description: w17 immediate-visibility: the filename of the most-recently-created document linked to this contract. Populated from the moment of upload (before any extraction stage runs), so a row with documentProcessingStatus=Uploaded already carries a recognisable filename. Null only for orphaned Contract shells whose last document was deleted.

One of Uploaded|Processing|NeedsReview|Completed|Failed|Rejected, or null for orphaned Contract shells. patch.summary: Record a human correction to one or more extracted Contract fields as a new version.
patch.description: Maps to CorrectContractAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/ContractsEndpointExtensions.cs, backed by ContractCorrectionService (task E02/F05/US01/T01, us-01-correction-history AC-1). Task E07/F03/US01/T01 (field-review-correction, ADR-020 screen 6) adds this operation and the sibling GET /api/contracts/{id}/corrections below -- see this document's own provenance paragraph for why. `corrections` accepts only the field names ContractCorrectionService.CorrectableFieldNames lists (type, status, currency, startDate, endDate, effectiveDate, cancellationDeadline, annualSpend, totalContractValue, autoRenewal, renewalTermMonths, paymentTerms, governingLaw); every value is that field's own canonical wire string (dates yyyy-MM-dd, booleans 'true'/'false', decimals/integers via InvariantCulture ToString()) -- ContractCorrectionService's own field table is the single source of truth for parsing/validation, this document does not re-validate. A key present with a JSON null clears an optional field (rejected for a required one, returned as 400); a key absent from the map leaves that field untouched. At least one supplied value must actually differ from the contract's current value, or the whole request fails as 400 (no-op corrections are rejected, never silently accepted). Same interim X-Tenant-Id header placeholder as every other operation above.

corrections.description: Field name (ContractCorrectionService.CorrectableFieldNames) -> new value (canonical wire string) or null (clear an optional field).

reason.description: Free-text reason, stored verbatim on every affected CorrectionHistory row and on the AuditEntry this write also produces.

200.description: Correction recorded as a new ContractVersion; at least one field actually changed.

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id header, non-GUID id, empty/unknown 'corrections' key, an unparsable value for its field's type, or every supplied value already matches the contract's current value.

Ordered newest-first per field (ContractCorrectionHistoryQueryService.cs's own OrderByDescending(CorrectedAt)) -- the first array entry for a given fieldName is always that field's latest correction. get.summary: Latest extraction evidence per contract field: page, span, confidence, quoted passage, model.
get.description: Maps to GetContractEvidenceAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/ContractsEndpointExtensions.cs, backed by Raffa.Documents.Contracts.Application.ContractEvidenceQueryService. Exposes the ExtractionEvidence trail the staged extraction pipeline has written since task E02/F01/US02/T01 (product spec §7.3 "every extracted fact carries source span + confidence") -- one entry per field, the newest evidence row winning, alphabetical by fieldName. `fieldName` is the same key PATCH /api/contracts/{id} accepts (currency, annualSpend, supplier, ...), plus `type` for the classification verdict (no page/span: it reads the whole document). `passage` is the sentence of the indexed page text around `sourceSpan` with the span's offsets, present only when the page text still contains the span -- never an approximated context. `box` (epic-23 feature-02, ADR-003 w18) is the phrase's pixel-space bounding rectangle on the rendered page image, or null for text-level highlight only; every row is null today because no writer populates the four geometry columns it is read from until epic-23 feature-04 ships. Each field carries a server-computed `decision` (`auto_accepted` | `human_accepted` | `review_required`). `autoAcceptThreshold` is emitted once per response so the web never hardcodes 90. The review screen's evidence pane and per-field confidence tags read this. A contract that exists but has no evidence returns 200 with `fields: []`.

200.description: Contract found for this tenant (possibly with zero evidence rows). autoAcceptThreshold is emitted once; fields may be empty.

autoAcceptThreshold.description: The raw confidence bar the server applied (0.90). Once per response so the web never hardcodes 90.

value.description: What the model proposed, verbatim -- not the contract's current (possibly corrected) value.

confidence.description: 0..1 as the model reported it; null when it reported none.

decision.description: Server-computed acceptance of this field. Never supplied by a caller.

sourcePage.description: 1-based page the span was read from; null when unknown.

sourceSpan.description: The literal text the fact was read from, as quoted by the model.

box.description: Pixel-space bounding box of this phrase on the rendered page image (the same page sourcePage names), from prebuilt-layout word geometry (ADR-017 w18) unioned over the phrase's words. Null for every document rasterized before this wave, or any page the OCR call returned no layout geometry for -- the viewer then falls back to the sourceSpan text-level highlight, never an error.

x.description: Left edge, in the rendered page image's pixel coordinate space.

y.description: Top edge, in the rendered page image's pixel coordinate space.

sourceFileName.description: File name of the source document, for the evidence card header.

passage.description: Sentence(s) of the indexed page text around the span; null when the span cannot be located.

highlightStart.description: Zero-based offset of sourceSpan inside passage.

modelId.description: Model id of the extraction job that proposed this fact (brief §8 traceability).

This document does not yet expose a GET read-back of the same row: RenewalActionService.GetActionAsync exists but its own doc comment says 'no HTTP route calls this yet'. web/src/routes/renewals/renewalActionStore.ts documents the client-side, session-scoped interim this drives -- the same kind of gap web/src/routes/signin/workspaceStore.ts and web/src/routes/documents/documentStore.ts already establish for their own missing-endpoint gaps.

No role gate -- any live tenant member reads (a non-member is 404, never 403, ADR-025 Rule B1). A bare JSON array, not { items: [...] }: this is a small, unpaginated, per-contract list, the same shape GET /api/audit already returns for the identical reason. Never a 404 for 'nothing upserted yet' -- a well-formed contract id with no rows is an honest 200 []; the only 404 cause is ICallerContext resolving the caller to a non-member of the tenant. Order: ICallerContext (401 no identity / 400 malformed tenant header / 404 not a member) -- then the Admin-or-Procurement role gate (403), before the route id is even parsed -- then the id's GUID format (400) -- then the tick itself. 404 when pointKey names no existing row for this (tenant, contract): this route never creates one (client-architect's 'never invent a point'). Unconditional tick: an already-Done or previously-Superseded row both become/stay Done -- there is no un-tick route. Task E29/F04/US01/T01 (todo-web) is the first web caller.

get.summary: Procurement-homepage KPI row: spend/contracts/renewals plus the three savings buckets.
get.description: Maps to GetSavingsKpisAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/SavingsKpiEndpointExtensions.cs (task E04/F03/US01/T01, us-01-savings-kpis AC-1; product spec section 10.1's six-row KPI table; task E20/F01/US01/T01, NW-72, verified-money read). Task E08/F02/US01/T01 (savings-home, ADR-020 screen 9) adds this operation -- the fifth web epic to extend this document (see this document's own info.description 'repeating chore' provenance paragraph). 'Annual spend analyzed'/'Contracts analyzed' come from Raffa.Documents.Contracts (PortfolioQueryService.GetAnalysisSummaryAsync); 'Savings identified'/'Savings in progress' come from Raffa.Savings opportunity estimate ranges (SavingsKpiQueryService.GetSummaryAsync); 'Savings realized' is verified money grouped by currency from RealizedSavings rows (currency/amount/count), never the estimate band; 'Upcoming renewals' reuses GET /api/renewals's own auto-renewing candidate query rather than rebuilding the full pipeline just to count it (see that endpoint's own C# doc comment for the full reasoning) -- this operation never calls Raffa.Benchmark directly, so a benchmark-provider outage cannot surface as a distinct HTTP status here; the web client's own 'benchmark provider unreachable' Home-screen state (screens.md #9) is this call failing for any reason, not a status code this endpoint reserves for that cause specifically. Each spend/savings figure is grouped by currency, never summed across currencies (this codebase has no currency-conversion service) -- an empty array is the honest zero-contracts/zero-opportunities answer, never a fabricated zero-currency row.

get.summary: The caller's last N conversations (rail resume list).
get.description: Maps to GetConversationsAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/ConversationsEndpointExtensions.cs, backed by ConversationService.ListRecentAsync (task E13/F05/US01/T02, us-01-conversations; R-CONV-02 'the rail shows the user's last 5 conversations, resume by click'). Bare array response, not a {items,totalCount} envelope -- there is no paging concept for 'my last N conversations'. Optional ?take= overrides ConversationService.DefaultRecentLimit (5); web/src/api/client.ts#listConversations never sends it, always taking the backend default. Caller identity (task E13/F09/US01/T04, ADR-022/OQ-askv2-005/R-CONV-03): X-User-Id is required in addition to X-Tenant-Id on every operation under /api/conversations -- ConversationsEndpointExtensions.TryResolveUserId prefers an authenticated ClaimsPrincipal's subject claim (the ADR-010 end state; never true today, nothing wires AddAuthentication yet) and otherwise requires this header, the MSAL account username, non-authoritative until the API JWT lands. A 400 covers a missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id, a missing X-User-Id, or a malformed ?take=.

parameters.name: X-User-Id
parameters.description: MSAL account username (ADR-022 Day-1 posture; OQ-askv2-005; R-CONV-03). Non-authoritative -- replaced by the token subject once ADR-010's API JWT lands. Required on every /api/conversations* operation.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Overrides ConversationService.DefaultRecentLimit (5) when supplied; must be a positive integer.

scopeContractId.description: Set when this conversation was opened from Contract 360 'Ask about it' (/ask?scope=); null for a plain new chat.

post.summary: Starts a new conversation, optionally scoped to a contract.
post.description: Maps to PostConversationAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/ConversationsEndpointExtensions.cs, backed by ConversationService.CreateAsync (task E13/F05/US01/T02; R-CONV-01/R-CONV-02; ADR-024 'the global Ask bar always opens a new chat'). Request body is ConversationsEndpointExtensions.CreateConversationRequest, hand-written in web/src/api/client.ts (the generator does not parse requestBody -- see this document's own 'Codegen tool choice' paragraph): `{ scopeContractId? }`, a GUID string. An absent/blank scopeContractId opens a plain new chat (title defaults to 'New chat' until the first question lands); a well-formed one scopes it to that contract (Contract 360's 'Ask about it', /ask?scope=<contractId>). A malformed (non-GUID) scopeContractId is a 400, not silently dropped. Same X-Tenant-Id/X-User-Id pair as GET /api/conversations above.

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id or X-User-Id header, or a non-GUID scopeContractId.

get.summary: One conversation, with every turn, oldest first.
get.description: Maps to GetConversationAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/ConversationsEndpointExtensions.cs, backed by ConversationService.GetAsync (task E13/F05/US01/T02; R-CONV-02 AC-1 'resuming a conversation renders past turns with citation cards and actions still clickable'). 404, never 403, whether {id} does not exist, belongs to another tenant (RLS backstop, ADR-009), or belongs to another user of the same tenant (an application-level filter -- ConversationService's own doc comment: 'RLS has no per-user predicate') -- one honest outcome, never a distinguishing signal (AC-1/AC-2 'another user/tenant cannot list or read the conversation'). Each message's citations/actions are the identical shapes POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages returns (duplicated, not $ref'd -- this document has no $ref/oneOf support, see its own 'Codegen tool choice' paragraph) EXCEPT a stored message never carries `followUps` -- ConversationMessage has no such column (ConversationsEndpointExtensions.ToMessageResponse's own field list), so a resumed conversation's past Raffa turns render without follow-up chips, an honest, real limitation, not an oversight.

200.description: The conversation and its messages, oldest first.

markdown.description: The caller's own question verbatim for a 'you' turn; Raffa's answerMarkdown for a 'raffa' turn.

corpus.description: Usually 'tenant' | 'market' | 'raffa' (requirements.md §6 / R-WEB-04's three-corpus citation-badge vocabulary). Backend truth (Raffa.Chat.Application.Reply.ReplyCitation.Corpus's own doc comment: 'Echoes PackItem.Corpus') admits a fourth internal value, 'calc' (a deterministic-calculator-derived fact -- a renewal date, a negotiation lever, a criticality score -- Raffa.Chat.Application.Pack.PackCorpus.Calc), with no remapping step anywhere before the wire; confirmed by reading backend/src/Raffa.Api/AskCopilotService.cs's own PackItem constructions for 'when-you-must-move'/lever/target/criticality items, which set a real /contracts/{id} Href despite PackItem.Href's own doc comment claiming Href is null for PackCorpus.Calc. Left a plain string (not `enum`) to stay honest about this observed gap rather than declare a fourth badge variant replyTypes.ts does not have; web/src/routes/ask/askViewModel.ts#toCitationCorpus folds an unrecognised value into 'tenant' (the closer honest bucket -- a calculator fact is always about this tenant's own contract, never a market/feature fact).

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id or X-User-Id header, or a non-GUID id in the route.

404.description: No such conversation for this tenant and caller (unknown id, another tenant's, or another user's -- one honest outcome, see this operation's own description).

post.summary: Asks a question in an existing conversation; runs the Ask engine and returns the reply.
post.description: Maps to PostConversationMessageAsync in backend/src/Raffa.Api/ConversationsEndpointExtensions.cs -- the one endpoint that actually runs the Ask engine (Raffa.Api.AskCopilotService.AskAsync, task E13/F06/US01/T01), then persists both the caller's question and Raffa's reply (ConversationService.AppendMessageAsync) before wire-shaping the same object back (shared with POST /api/chat/query's own alias, ConversationsEndpointExtensions.AskAndAppendAsync). Request body `{ question }` (ConversationsEndpointExtensions.PostConversationMessageRequest, hand-written client-side, see this document's 'Codegen tool choice' paragraph). Reply shape is ADR-024 §6 / inputs/requirements.md §6, kind decides the layout: `answer` (markdown + citations + actions + followUps), `abstain` (a true-insufficiency reply, citations/actions/followUps empty), `redirect` (greeting/off-domain/needs_document, one CTA), `refusal` (legal, one CTA). `actions[].kind` is 'navigate' | 'upload' (Raffa.Chat.Application.Capabilities.CopilotActionKind) -- inputs/requirements.md §6's own JSON example shows 'primary'/'secondary' instead, an illustrative visual-priority label the real backend never emits; web/src/routes/ask/askViewModel.ts maps the real navigate/upload/index-ordered actions onto ReplyAction's presentational primary/secondary at the UI boundary (replyTypes.ts, task E13/F09/US01/T02, is out of this task's file scope to change). See GET /api/conversations/{id} above for why `corpus` is a plain string, not a 3-value enum. 404 under the identical tenant/user/unknown-id rule GET /api/conversations/{id} documents.

200.description: The routed reply -- always 200 once the conversation is confirmed to exist, per ChatEndpointExtensions' own long-standing convention for this same composition root; an abstain/redirect/refusal is a successful, honest answer, not an error status.

answerMarkdown.description: Narrated prose with inline [n] markers; empty for abstain/redirect/refusal? no -- redirect/refusal still carry warm prose here (R-ASK-07); only truly nothing to narrate is empty.

corpus.description: See GET /api/conversations/{id} above's identical citations[].corpus for the full 'tenant/market/raffa, occasionally calc' provenance note.

href.description: A tenant citation's own destination -- observed backend behaviour (AskCopilotService.cs's PackItem constructions) always sets this to the bare `/contracts/{contractId}`, never `/contracts/{contractId}?clause=...`, despite inputs/requirements.md §6's own illustrative example showing a `?clause=` suffix. web/src/routes/ask/askViewModel.ts appends `?page={page}` itself (when `page` is present) before navigating, reusing web/src/routes/contracts/contract360/contract360ViewModel.ts#resolveHighlightedClauseId's existing page-based clause lookup -- a `?clause=` deep link cannot be built client-side today because no citation field carries a raw clauseId (R-ASK-08 'no guids ever rendered' -- consistent with that, not a client oversight).

400.description: Missing/invalid X-Tenant-Id or X-User-Id header, a non-GUID id in the route, or a blank 'question'.

404.description: No such conversation for this tenant and caller.

get.summary: The versioned, static capability catalog.

The server-side role filter is deleted; hiding an admin-gated chip from a non-Admin is client work deferred to W17. web/src/routes/ask/index.tsx / web/src/components/ask-bar/askSuggestions.ts (task E13/F09/US01/T04) read only `capabilities[].exampleQuestions` for the two-chip suggestions this task adds; `CapabilityCatalog.SuggestionsFor`'s own richer per-screen/supplier-templated chip copy (app.jsx `chipsFor`/`c360Chips`) is a backend-internal helper with no HTTP surface at all -- this task reproduces the two prototype-verbatim supplier-templated strings client-side for the Contract-360-scoped case (askViewModel.ts) rather than inventing a new endpoint for them.

200.description: The full catalog. Every row carries its own roleGate label; the server does not filter.
